correctness.rationale: For any two rotations, cross-boundary ordered-pair counts differ by c_a s_b-c_b s_a, vanishing exactly for proportional segment content. Gcd divisibility forces collision distances to be multiples of N/d, proving the lower bound and periodic minimum. At least three monochromatic runs rule out all proper balanced arcs in a grouped word, yielding full maximum N. Adjacent exchanges modify only one centered-prefix vector, so the class-count change is at most one, proving every intermediate value. These arguments cover all positive vectors and the gcd-one boundary. The independent direct-vs-prefix computational checker passed 18,666 fixed-content words; no finite test is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Provides the full attainable spectrum for arbitrary positive fixed content and arbitrarily large alphabets with at least three letters, a natural complete classification of circular 2-binomial signatures. It explains the nonbinary full-distinguishability endpoint by a three-run obstruction and yields constructive witnesses by sorting. This is not a routine calculation of one finite instance, an alphabet rename, or a claimed novelty for the binary result.
